speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your condition, could you describe the nature and severity of your flank pain, and did you complete the full course of antibiotics for your sinusitis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning when you urinate, and have you noticed any changes in the color or clarity of your urine? Also, do you have any nausea or vomiting associated with these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of a rash with amoxicillin and subsequent flank pain with fever, I suspect a possible interstitial nephritis or a kidney infection. Do you have any back tenderness when I press on your flank, and have you noticed any changes in your urine output or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of leukocyturia with a negative bacterial culture, along with eosinophilic cells in the urine, strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis likely triggered by the antibiotics. I need to assess your kidney function to confirm the severity of the injury. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine
REQUEST TEST: Blood_Urea_Nitrogen

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatinine and BUN confirm acute kidney injury, which, combined with the sterile pyuria and urine eosinophils following antibiotic use, points to drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
